rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act: grounds and notice to quit (subsections l-r)
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict only for grounds listed in the Anti-Eviction Act. These include owner occupancy or sale to an occupying buyer (2 months' notice to quit, no suit until the lease expires), end of employment-based tenancy (3 days), and certain drug, assault, theft or trafficking offenses (3 days; suit within 2 years).
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the landlord may file a suit for eviction.
rules.key_value: Notice to quit: 3 days (employment, drug, assault, theft offenses); 2 months (owner occupancy/sale)
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings are covered separately by N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2.

unverifiable_exemptions: rooming/boarding houses and public housing follow separate rules

rules.title: Evictions in owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants in landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only by court order, and only for listed causes such as holdover, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, damage or rule violations. Notice to quit is 3 months (at-will or year-to-year), 1 month (month-to-month), or 3 days for disorderly, destructive or rule-violating conduct.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction.
rules.key_value: 3-month / 1-month / 3-day notice to quit depending on tenancy and cause

rules.title: Penalties for eviction law violations
rules.requirement: A landlord who evicts to personally occupy a unit must occupy it for at least six months. If the unit is instead used by another tenant or converted, the landlord owes triple damages plus fees. For removal from residential use, the property must stay non-residential for 5 years, with a civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months.
rules.key_value: 6 months owner occupancy; 5 years no residential use; treble damages; up to $10,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Three times damages plus attorney fees and costs; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation

rules.title: Reprisal protections for tenants exercising civil rights
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict, substantially alter lease terms, or refuse to renew a lease because a tenant enforced rights, made a good-faith complaint to authorities, organized or joined a tenant organization, or refused retaliatory lease changes. The tenant may sue for damages.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights
rules.key_value: Ban on retaliatory eviction, lease alteration or non-renewal

rules.title: Foreclosure tenant protections (Foreclosure Fairness Act)
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. A buyer who wants to occupy the unit must give a 90-day notice to quit after any lease ends. New owners must send tenants notices within 10 business days, and may not pressure tenants to accept buyout offers.
rules.quoted_span: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey.
rules.key_value: 90-day notice to quit; notice within 10 business days of sale

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act
rules.requirement: Eligible seniors (62+), permanently disabled tenants, and certain disabled veterans in buildings being converted to condominium or cooperative may be protected from eviction for up to 40 years. They must meet income limits and apply within about 60 days.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00

requires_unknown_facts: building is being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership
tenant is senior, disabled or qualifying veteran

parsed.doc_summary: Part 4 of the NJ DCA Truth-in-Renting guide. It covers the last Anti-Eviction Act grounds, owner-occupied 2-3 family evictions, penalties, reprisal, foreclosure protections and senior protected tenancy. All six records are just_cause_eviction. The rest is contact directories.
